flagged_runs.reason: fabricated a release date for a version that was never tagged (latest tag is v0.6.1) and whose tagging would auto-publish to PyPI. Reverted to 0.6.1 / 2026-06-29 before any commit; never entered history.

false compliance metadata: those docs carry their own dates (2026-06-29 / 2026-06-02) and describe v0.5/v0.6 coverage, so the relabel asserted an audit that never happened. Reverted before committing.

overclaiming gate: asserted 'doc_version <= tree_version', which PASSES the exact bad 0.7.0 relabel when tree is 0.7.0 (0.7.0 <= 0.7.0). It did not block the fabrication it was described as blocking. Removed in R2.

flagged_runs.reason: encoded a release-cadence policy as a unit test. This repo has legitimately let hive-cpp lag (at tag v0.6.0, hive-cpp was 0.5.0 while root was 0.6.0). Narrowed in R2 to internal consistency only.
read as released ('This release') and pointed at a version absent from every index. Retitled '(pending — not yet released)' and gated the install command behind 'When released:' in R2.

flagged_runs.artifact: install blocks in README / USAGE / MCP_SETUP / HARNESS_SETUP / CONTRIBUTING / harness-omp / harness-pi / NORMAL-PEOPLE / WHATS_NEW; RELEASE_NOTES v0.6.1 'PyPI distribution'
flagged_runs.reason: committed at b2f66e8 and earlier: guidance pointed at `pip install hive-agent-memory`, which 404s on PyPI (verified with a passing control), and the v0.6.1 note claimed distribution that never occurred. Replaced with source installs and a corrected note in a827980.

flagged_runs.artifact: every CPU CI job red on main while local verify.sh was green
flagged_runs.reason: two independent defects introduced by this session, both invisible to a local run on Python 3.12 with untracked files present: (a) tests/test_version_consistency.py imported tomllib (3.11+) while CI runs a 3.10 matrix job -> collection error; (b) oracle/solution.patch was gitignored but task.json references it and --verify-tasks (CI + verify.sh) requires it -> 'no solution_patch' x12 in a fresh clone. Tell: `gh run view <id> --log-failed` showed ModuleNotFoundError: tomllib and the 12 missing patches; a fresh `git clone` reproduced (b) locally. Fixed in adabeea; verified by cloning fresh and running --verify-tasks (12/12).

flagged_runs.artifact: every push to main permanently 'queued', never a CI result
flagged_runs.reason: the gpu job targets [self-hosted, gpu, cuda] and 0 runners are registered, so it was never schedulable; continue-on-error only forgives a job that runs. PR runs skip the job and complete, which is why PRs looked healthy and main never did. Tell: `gh api .../actions/runners` -> total_count 0, and every main run's CPU jobs finished success while the run-level status stayed queued. Fixed in c4956de by gating both self-hosted jobs on the ENABLE_SELF_HOSTED_CI variable.

flagged_runs.artifact: benchmarks/cpu_router.joblib — the shipped trained CPU policy
flagged_runs.reason: the artifact was fitted on 19 features while featurize() produces 47, so CPURouterPolicy.predict() raised 'ValueError: X has 47 features, but RandomForestClassifier is expecting 19' on the FIRST decision of every episode. An arm run with --policy trained therefore records 0/N resolved and 0 LLM calls — a silent total failure that reads as a bad policy rather than a stale artifact. Tell: running --policy trained (not --policy rule) crashed every episode; the traceback named the width mismatch. Fixed by retraining on rebuilt trajectories and by a fail-closed width check in CPURouterPolicy.load().

closed_levers.detail: Syncing every '0.6.1' string to '0.7.0' asserts a release/audit that did not happen: citation.cff and the compliance/runbook/SOC2 docs assert a RELEASED or AUDITED state and must stay at the last actual release. Only mechanically-coupled build metadata follows the tree version.

Encoding the release-cadence decision as an equality assertion (hive-cpp == root, Helm == root) freezes a maintainer policy as a test; the repo has drifted before by choice (v0.6.0: cpp 0.5.0 vs root 0.6.0). Tests assert only internal consistency; cross-artifact alignment is a review item.

Cutting a v0.7.0 tag is not a way to 'finish' a version bump: release.yml runs the PyPI publish job on tag, so tagging attempts an external publish — and the existing v0.6.1 tag with a PyPI 404 shows the job did not (does not) guarantee publication. It requires separate authorization, not bookkeeping.
Forcing document version stamps to equal the working-tree version fabricates a released/audited state. Live guidance docs (USAGE) may track the tree; attestation docs must not lead it.
A gate written alongside a fix can encode the fix's own claim rather than the invariant (see F3). Validate a gate against the exact failure mode it claims to catch — a seeded mismatch exposed it.

verify.sh ran one interpreter (3.12) on a machine that already had untracked files, so it was blind to a 3.10-only import error and to a file that only exists because it was never committed. Release-readiness needs a fresh-clone run and a real CI conclusion, not just a local gate.

continue-on-error forgives a job that RUNS and fails; it does nothing for a job that can never be scheduled. A job pinned to a non-existent runner label wedges the whole run forever. Gate such jobs on a variable, or the workflow's status is never a signal.

a serialized model that no longer matches its featurizer fails at call time, not load time, and in an eval harness that failure is swallowed into 'unresolved'. Gate the artifact: a saved policy must declare the feature width it was trained on and load() must refuse a mismatch.

training a router on the same tasks it is scored on measures memorisation, not generalisation. Rebuilt trajectories are split so the hard tier stays held out: the retrained policy learns from the 16 non-hard tasks only.

harness_invalid_runs.what: a fresh-venv install smoke that appeared to prove a packaging bug (`setuptools>=83` unsatisfiable)
harness_invalid_runs.tell: the smoke used the system `python3` = 3.9.6, below the project's `requires-python >=3.10`; setuptools 83+ declares `Requires-Python: >=3.10`, so pip correctly found no candidate
harness_invalid_runs.resolution: rerun under Python 3.12.13 (supported): install succeeds -> NO packaging bug. pyproject/CI were NOT changed; the pin `setuptools>=83` is satisfiable on the supported range
harness_invalid_runs.recorded_because: a failed measurement must not be laundered into a defect report
